cells.tense: Right now you're letting go of things on purpose, one at a time, as you see through them.
cells.ask: Before you start anything today, pick the one small practice you'd keep even if nobody ever noticed, and do it for fifteen minutes with the timer where you can see it.
cells.core:
Whatever you're clearing away at the moment, you're clearing it because you actually saw through it, not because it got too heavy. You notice the moment a thing stops being true, and you let it go when the moment comes, which is why people keep bringing you the question they can't answer themselves.

That's the same attention you'd bring to a practice chosen on purpose. Pick the one small thing you'd keep doing if no one ever saw it, and give it a quarter of an hour today with the timer in view. This kind of practice isn't straining; it hands back a read on yourself that you can't get from thinking about it. The cost is real, though — a thing you choose to keep is easier to drop than a life that forces it on you, and you'll feel that the first day you miss.
cells.sheetLine: You let go of what stopped being true — now pick one thing to keep.
cells.verb: letting what's built on a false premise come down
cells.place: the part of you that knows what to attend to before you can say why

cells.tense: You're already bracing for what comes next, pulling things down before they've fallen on their own.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you kept from a practice that didn't survive, and ask them how it went for them.
cells.core:
You can feel something wobble and your hands are on it before it decides anything — the ending gets run ahead of the event, so nothing gets to stand long enough to be looked at. Some of what you're dismantling hasn't actually failed yet; you got there first.

Put one piece of what you found in front of someone else and ask what it was like on their end. Meaning only holds when it's handed between people, and handing it over is slower than the wrecking, which is the point. What comes back may be quieter than the clearing you're used to, but it's something you can stand on for more than a week.

cells.tense: You're still holding up something that stopped standing a while back, and the work of holding has become the whole job.
cells.ask: Write down the three things you're keeping going right now, and pick one to stop maintaining for this week — one you can leave without consequences piling up.
cells.core:
Somewhere in your ordinary week you're holding something up that already came apart, and the effort that goes into it is the effort that used to go to seeing what matters. You're keeping a shape that isn't there anymore, and the keeping has gone quiet enough that it feels like normal life.

Give one of those structures a container instead — put down in writing the three things you're keeping going, then let one of them go quiet for the week. Structure that serves what it holds makes the ground clear enough to know what to attend to; you find that out by clearing one thing and watching what your attention does. The hard part is that if you stop, you might find out you no longer know what the structure was for, and that's worth knowing too.

cells.tense: You're in the middle of a shift right now and you're talking about it as if it were happening to you.
cells.ask: Take ten minutes today and write one sentence naming the thing you actually want next — not the good reason, the want.
cells.core:
Things around you have already started coming apart, and you keep describing it as a run of bad luck or a phase. You're the one who saw it first, which is why it's happening at all, but you keep filing that as something that happened to you rather than something you did.

Write one plain sentence about what you want next — the actual want, not the reason that makes it sound sensible. Direction that starts from what you care about moves differently than direction from duty, and a want you've said once is much harder to keep calling an accident. Starting from what you want may make the ending feel chosen rather than suffered, and that change is the whole thing.
